note: Attention is also the interjection/warning 'watch out!/careful!', which should be represented because interjection POS is already listed.
proposed_english: attention; vigilance; care; watch out!; careful!

note: The current gloss omits the basic adjective 'strong' and noun 'fort/stronghold', despite listing adjective/adverb/noun POS.
proposed_english: strong; powerful; loud; strongly; very; fort; stronghold

note: 'Shar (shari'a)' is unrelated dictionary contamination. Chéri means cherished/beloved and, substantivally, darling/sweetheart.

Important is normally the adjective 'important/significant/considerable'; the same form can technically be the present participle of importer, so either the participle must be labeled or omitted. For learner clarity, keep it explicit but secondary.
proposed_english: important; significant; considerable; importing (present participle of importer, context-dependent)

note: Voici is a presentative expression ('here is/are'), not a preposition. 'Ago' occurs only in special time constructions and should not be the primary gloss.
proposed_english: here is; here are; this is; these are

note: Partie does not ordinarily mean an English social 'party'. Core meanings are part/portion, game/match/round, and party/group in some formal contexts.
proposed_english: part; portion; game; match; round; party/group (formal/context-dependent)

note: The foreign-currency 'lira/lire' dictionary material is irrelevant here. French lire is the verb 'to read'.
The current definition omits the basic meaning entirely. Eau means water; rain/body-fluid senses are contextual extensions.
Suite also commonly means continuation, rest/following part, and appears in tout de suite = immediately. The current result/sequel/sequence set is incomplete for learners.
proposed_english: continuation; sequence; sequel; following/rest; result; immediately (tout de suite)

note: Form-based homograph coverage should include vers as the plural of ver 'worm'; Larousse explicitly uses and defines plural vers in ordinary examples.
proposed_english: to/toward; around/about (time/date); verse; worms (plural of ver)

note: Battre centrally means beat/hit and can mean fight; 'beat up' is narrower than the basic verb.
proposed_english: to beat; to hit; to fight; to defeat; to thresh

note: Fin as a noun means end/finish; as an adjective it means fine/thin/refined/subtle. 'Kind, nice' is not a safe basic gloss.
proposed_english: end; finish; fine; thin; refined; subtle

note: Aide is the noun help/assistance or a helper/aide; English verb 'assist' should not be presented as the noun's direct basic gloss.
The current entry omits the basic verb 'touch' and gives 'try/try out', which is not a safe general meaning. Toucher also means affect and receive/earn money.
proposed_english: to touch; to affect; to reach; to receive/earn; touch (noun)

note: Devant means in front of/before and can be the noun 'front'. 'Outside' is not a normal equivalent. The same spelling can also be the present participle of devoir, but that is secondary.
proposed_english: in front of; before; front; owing/having to (present participle of devoir, rare/context-dependent)

note: Prier means not only pray but also beg/request/ask politely, as in je vous prie.
proposed_english: to pray; to beg; to request; to ask politely

note: Cause is primarily the noun cause/reason/legal case, but the same form also represents finite/imperative forms of causer. The current POS lists only noun while mentioning an imperative.
proposed_english: cause; reason; legal case; causes/talks (form of causer); talk! (imperative, context-dependent)
proposed_pos: noun / finite verb form / imperative form

note: Poser also very commonly means to ask (a question) and to pose; these core learner uses are missing.
proposed_english: to put; to place; to set; to pose; to ask (a question); to install
